title: Edge proxy certificate rotation runbook
brief: Redwater Media's Platform team needs a runbook for rotating the TLS certificates on the 18 edge proxies, owned by Platform Security. Sections: "When to rotate", "Before you start", "Rotation steps", "Rollback" and "Escalation". When to rotate: when a certificate has 30 days or fewer left, which the CERT_EXPIRY_30D alert announces; the certificates cover 12 hostnames. Before you start: have the change record open, confirm no deploy is running in #deploys, and check that the internal CA is healthy. Rotation steps, in order, with sub-steps. 1 Confirm expiry: a) run openssl x509 -enddate -noout on the live certificate, b) compare with the alert. 2 Request the new certificate: a) run certctl request --profile edge-prod, b) check that the output lists all 12 hostnames. 3 Stage it on the canary proxy edge-canary-01 only: a) copy it to /etc/edge/certs/next, b) reload the proxy. 4 Verify the canary: a) openssl s_client -connect edge-canary-01:443 shows the new expiry date, b) handshake errors stay under 0.1 percent for 20 minutes. 5 Roll out to the other 17 proxies in batches of 3, waiting 5 minutes between batches. 6 Revoke the old certificate after 48 hours and record it in the change record. Readers must be told firmly never to delete the old private key before step 6. Rollback: the previous certificate stays in /etc/edge/certs/previous for 7 days; copy it back and reload. Escalation: page Platform Security if any proxy shows more than 2 percent handshake errors, and post in #platform-sec.

edit.request: Change the rollout to batches of 2 proxies, waiting 10 minutes between batches.
